# NOTES ON THE SOURCE TEXT (two books, kept separate)

Note: the system/environment material above is not part of either book; it's setup only.

---

## BOOK 1: The Man from Bar 20 (Clarence E. Mulford, Gutenberg 56154)

**Core cast**
- **Johnny Nelson** ("Dearly Beloved", "Kid"): two-gun cow-puncher from Bar-20 (Texas), formerly Tin Cup, Montana. Five ft ten, 160 lb, blue eyes, brown hair, left-handed writer, ambidextrous shooter. Wooden-handled flare-butt Frontier Colts, tied down. Sharpshooter with Sharp's Special rifle. Admits no master except Hopalong, who beats him on the draw barely.
- **Logan (John C. Logan)**: foreman/owner of CL ranch, Deepwater valley. Suspicious; hires Johnny believing he may be an identity match; letter from William Cassidy Sr. confirms Johnny's identity.
- **Pop Hayes**: proprietor of a Hastings saloon, sleeps much, dislikes riding. Parrot **Andrew Jackson ("Andy")** swears, likes whiskey, bites. Mare **Pepper** (black horse, Johnny's).
- **Charley James**: general store owner, Hastings; plays solitaire; fishing buddy with Pop.
- **Tom Quigley**: rustler leader; QE brand; lives in Twin Buttes valley (Rustler Creek, Quigley's valley, 13 miles long).
- **Jim Ackerman**: Quigley's gunman, expert with six-gun, cruel; Johnny kicks and humiliates him in Hastings; later shot by Johnny near Humpback Butte.
- **Art Fleming**, **Frank Holbrook**, **Nat Harrison**, **Ben Gates** (Benjamin Franklin Gates), **Purdy**, **Sanford**, **Cookie** (cook, coyote enemy), **Long Pete (Pete Carson)**: rustler/hand; Ackerman recruits him; Pete killed by Holbrook/Harrison ambush mistaking him for Nelson.
- **Luke Tedrue**: old scout, Remington .44 "Old Betsy," knife "Colonel Bowie"; comes to help Johnny.
- Hopalong, Red Connors, Buck, Skinny, Lanky, Pete Wilson, Tex Ewalt, Youbet Somes, Mary (Mrs. Hopalong), William Junior (kid, shot-gun promise).

**Events in order**
1. Johnny rides into country, singing "The Cowboy's Lament"; ambushed by unseen shooter near Twin Buttes; saves himself. Says "Dearly Beloved" to horse.
2. Hastings: Pop's saloon. Johnny asks for box of .45s; talks about jobs (Circle S, Long T/Smith, CL, Logan). Andy parrot attacks; Johnny flicks it. Pop warns Johnny looks like Logan.
3. CL ranch: Johnny hired after identity talk; Logan's letter from Cassidy; Johnny explains history of Bar-20 friends.
4. Logan explains rustling (cows vanishing up Little Canyon). Johnny plans to pose as ex-employee and prospect. Frog refrain: "Go 'round! Knee deep!"
5. Johnny starts prospecting; fake quarrel with Logan (blankets, cows, river); leaves CL. Buys outfit from Charley (axe "Little Gem," fishhooks gift). Finds gold at Devil's Gap; brook trout.
6. Builds cabin at Nelson's creek near Little Canyon. Discovers rustlers' ranch (stone houses, narrow canyon).
7. Night reconnaissance with Logan's rope; sees rustlers; nearly stopped by wolf; finds Pepper with saddle.
8. Council: Ackerman and Fleming ride to scout; Quigley plans to scare Johnny off; burn cabin, frame him.
9. Johnny's cabin "Vamose" sign; Hastings confrontation with Ackerman in street; Ackerman beaten/disarmed; Johnny takes Ackerman's ivory-handled gun.
10. Night skirmish: cabin burned; Gates tied up; Harrison and Fleming hit; cougar shot by Gates; Johnny gets clothes ruined.
11. Johnny camps; rustler herd raids; Quigley's crossing of Deepwater; cook's chickens.
12. Ackerman goes hunting Nelson; Long Pete joins Ackerman; Pete says he knows where Nelson is.
13. Johnny found at Humpback butte; Ackerman shot dead by Johnny (Ackerman's horse gets loose and nearly wrecks plan).
14. Johnny moves camp to southern Twin; Quigley and rustlers ambush him on the wall trail. Johnny hides; rustlers burn fire.
15. Johnny throws rocks; grizzly and snake episodes; Holbrook killed in later fight; Fleming shot by Johnny's rifle; Sanford fights; Fleming's trousers and skunk episode (Purdy, Holbrook, Fleming).
16. Johnny shoots Quigley's arm during parley; Quigley offers Johnny a share; Johnny refuses.
17. Luke Tedrue arrives; Johnny and Luke take QE; Gates shot; Quigley fights Johnny in creek and is killed; Johnny says "All but th' cows."

**Ending (quote):** Johnny: "Are they _all_ gone under?" — "All but th' cows," sighed Johnny.

## BOOK 2: Betty Wales, Sophomore (Margaret Warde / Edith Dunton, Gutenberg 6432)

**Core cast**
- **Betty Wales**: sophomore, Belden House; from Cleveland; brother **Will** and sister **Nan** (Nan on European trip); little green lizard ornament; fond of fun; roommate **Helen Chase Adams** (awkward, becomes athletic/serious; writes basketball song "accepted"; T. Reed her friend; roommate change to T. Reed at end).
- **Eleanor Watson**: former snob, returns sophomore; brother **Jim** (Cornell), father **Judge Watson**; writes story copied from "The Quiver" (Richard Blake) and gets into Dramatic Club; eventually resigns.
- **Madeline Ayres**: "girl from Bohemia" (New York), class secretary, speaks many languages; friend of Mary, Betty; knows Dick Blake from Paris.
- **Mary Brooks**: Chapin house, practical jokes; Roberta Lewis (shy, quiet; father in California); Nita Reese; Babe (Babbie) and Bob Parker ("the B's"); Katherine Kittredge (Kankakee); Rachel Morrison (quiet, off campus, white house); Dorothy King (senior, business manager of "Argus"); Frances West (editor-in-chief "Argus", poet); Beatrice Egerton (exchange editor/president Dramatic Club, flippant); Jean Eastman and Polly Eastman; Dora Carlson (Ohio farm girl, Market Street, sugaring-off party); Emily Davis (Aid society, beneficiary); Christy Mason (Students' Commission, away with mother); Marion Lawrence/Lustig; Miss Ferris (faculty, tea); Miss Hale ("Ethel," Nan's friend); Miss Raymond (theme instructor); Miss Stuart (president/faculty); Mrs. Chapin; Mrs. Cass (Belden matron); Alice Waite.
- **Richard (Dick) Blake**: editor of "The Quiver" (Fulton St., New York), plays cynical; lectures at Harding on "Tendencies of the Modern Drama."

**Events in order**
1. Betty moves into Belden House; Madeline Ayres visits (green vase advice). Nita and the B's late-night snack.
2. Sophomore reception: Eleanor takes Dora Carlson (Betty's arranged swap); Eleanor's violets. Jean's comments.
3. Republican parade (Mary, Madeline, Nita "defeated candidate"); Hallowe'en; Helen joins gym; Mary's ideas about societies.
4. Eleanor's theme copied from "The Quiver" (story); Miss Raymond praises; Eleanor refuses to let "Argus" print; Dorothy angrily forces.
5. Harding Aid "Show": Madeline's ideas; Animal Fair; circus; Eleanor's gypsy-reading.
6. Hallowe'en/ambition talk with Ethel Hale; Nan and Will visit; Will and Mary; Eleanor declines dinner.
7. Christmas: Roberta visits Betty's Cleveland home; midyears; Katherine's tea; Eleanor's coolness.
8. Society elections: Bob Parker (Dramatic Club), Marion Lustig, Eleanor (Dramatic Club) and Helen's song; sugar-party/Emily Davis.
9. February: Lucy Merrifield appoints Betty to Students' Commission (Christy away). Miss Ferris: "that won't be new work."
10. Dorothy's "Argus" sanctum: Richard Blake's letter (Feb 2) found in zoology bulletin board; Frances replies; Blake claims Eleanor's story copied.
11. Dorothy begs Betty to go to NY; Betty decides after talk with Eleanor. Madeline reveals she read "The Quiver."
12. Betty goes to NY during blizzard; meets Blake; Blake lectures at Harding later; Eleanor's dinner with Dr. Blake's "moral tone" talk.
13. Basketball: Helen's song prize; Eleanor's song rejected; Eleanor's theme story (Western story) returns from Miss Raymond.
14. Dora's sugaring-off; fortune-cookie insult; Eleanor's resignation discussion with Miss Ferris ("Paradise" woods walk).
15. May Day: Eleanor resigns Dramatic Club (accepted one year); Bob loses song; Helen's song; Betty elected Dramatic Club; eight pins.
16. End: Betty and Helen split (Helen and T. Reed to room together); Dorothy's successor Betty; closing "here's to junior year."
